the-chronicles-of-narnia.title: The Chronicles of Narnia
the-chronicles-of-narnia.summary: Children from our world stumble into Narnia, a land of talking animals and old magic, and help its true rulers against dark powers. Seven linked books follow Narnia from its creation to its end.
the-chronicles-of-narnia.note: Box-set or whole-series entry; dates span 1950-1956.

the-chronicles-of-narnia-7-books.title: The Chronicles of Narnia (7 books)
the-chronicles-of-narnia-7-books.summary: The complete seven-book set about the land of Narnia, from its creation to its last days. Children from our world are called in turn to help the great lion Aslan.
characters: Eustace Scrubb — whiny cousin turned hero
the-chronicles-of-narnia-7-books.note: Box set; same series as the other Narnia entries; books published 1950-1956.

the-voyage-of-the-dawn-treader-chronicle.title: The Voyage of the Dawn Treader
the-voyage-of-the-dawn-treader-chronicle.summary: Lucy, Edmund and their sour cousin Eustace sail with King Caspian to the eastern edge of the world in search of seven lost lords. Strange islands, sea serpents and a dragon test them all.
the-voyage-of-the-dawn-treader-chronicle.series: The Chronicles of Narnia (book 3 by publication)
the-voyage-of-the-dawn-treader-chronicle.note: Title in notebook includes series label; corrected.

the-silver-chair.title: The Silver Chair
the-silver-chair.summary: Eustace and Jill Pole are sent by Aslan to find the lost Prince Rilian of Narnia. Their journey takes them across giant-haunted moors to a dark realm deep underground.
the-silver-chair.setting: Narnia, northern wilds and the Underland

the-horse-and-his-boy.title: The Horse and His Boy
the-horse-and-his-boy.summary: A boy named Shasta and a talking horse, Bree, flee the southern land of Calormen toward Narnia. On the way they meet a proud girl, Aravis, and learn of a danger threatening the north.
the-horse-and-his-boy.setting: Calormen, Archenland and Narnia, during the Pevensies' reign

prince-caspian.title: Prince Caspian
prince-caspian.summary: The Pevensies are pulled back to Narnia, now centuries later and ruled by usurpers. They join young Prince Caspian and the hidden Old Narnians to win back the land.
prince-caspian.setting: Narnia, many centuries after the Pevensies' first reign

the-magician-s-nephew.title: The Magician's Nephew
the-magician-s-nephew.summary: Digory and Polly are tricked into magic rings that carry them between worlds. They witness a dying world and the birth of Narnia, and learn where the wardrobe and the lamp-post came from.
the-magician-s-nephew.setting: London 1900 and the creation of Narnia

the-lion-the-witch-and-the-wardrobe.title: The Lion, the Witch and the Wardrobe
the-lion-the-witch-and-the-wardrobe.summary: Four evacuated siblings find a wardrobe leading to Narnia, locked in endless winter under the White Witch. With help from the lion Aslan they work to end her rule.
characters: Lucy Pevensie — first to find Narnia
the-lion-the-witch-and-the-wardrobe.setting: Narnia and an English country house, WWII

the-last-battle.title: The Last Battle
the-last-battle.summary: A false Aslan appears in Narnia's last days and King Tirian struggles to expose the deceit. The story brings the series to its close.

out-of-the-silent-planet.title: Out of the Silent Planet
out-of-the-silent-planet.summary: Cambridge philologist Ransom is kidnapped and taken to Mars, which its inhabitants call Malacandra. There he meets three very different peoples and discovers a world not at all what he feared.
out-of-the-silent-planet.note: Adult-leaning; included as family read-aloud for older readers.

perelandra.title: Perelandra
perelandra.summary: Ransom is sent to Venus, a world of floating islands where a young woman faces a temptation. A familiar villain follows him there.
characters: The Lady — innocent queen of Venus
perelandra.note: Adult-leaning; second of the Space Trilogy.

a-tale-of-two-cities-adapted-by-patricia.title: A Tale of Two Cities
a-tale-of-two-cities-adapted-by-patricia.summary: A simplified retelling of Dickens's story of London and Paris before and during the French Revolution. A family and two men who look alike are swept up in danger.
a-tale-of-two-cities-adapted-by-patricia.note: Adapted edition; adapter name could not be verified online. Original 1859.

a-christmas-carol.title: A Christmas Carol
a-christmas-carol.summary: Miserly Ebenezer Scrooge is visited by his dead partner and three spirits on Christmas Eve. They show him the cost of his coldness and the warmth he has missed.

a-tale-of-two-cities.title: A Tale of Two Cities
a-tale-of-two-cities.summary: Set in London and Paris during the French Revolution, the novel follows a physician freed from prison, his daughter, and two men whose fates cross. It is about sacrifice, resurrection and the price of revolution.

great-expectations.title: Great Expectations
great-expectations.summary: Orphan Pip, raised by his sister and her blacksmith husband, comes into mysterious wealth and moves to London. He learns who his friends truly are.
characters: Pip — humble boy with great hopes
great-expectations.setting: Kent marshes and London, early 19th century

bleak-house.title: Bleak House
bleak-house.summary: A never-ending lawsuit entangles many lives in Victorian London. Orphan Esther Summerson, her guardian and a web of secrets are drawn together.

the-old-curiosity-shop.title: The Old Curiosity Shop
the-old-curiosity-shop.summary: Young Nell Trent and her grandfather flee a cruel moneylender and wander across England. The dwarf Quilp pursues them.
the-old-curiosity-shop.illustrator: George Cattermole and Hablot K. Browne

the-great-brain.title: The Great Brain
the-great-brain.summary: Narrated by J.D., this tells of his clever older brother Tom, who uses his wits to make money and fix problems in a small Utah town. Many of his schemes help others, and many pay Tom.

more-adventures-of-the-great-brain.title: More Adventures of the Great Brain
more-adventures-of-the-great-brain.summary: Tom Fitzgerald is up to more clever tricks in 1890s Utah, with J.D. as his reluctant partner. Some schemes pay off, and some do not.

the-great-brain-at-the-academy.title: The Great Brain at the Academy
the-great-brain-at-the-academy.summary: Tom is sent off to a Catholic boarding school in Salt Lake City, where his schemes meet stiffer opposition. Back home J.D. misses him despite himself.

the-great-brain-reforms.title: The Great Brain Reforms
the-great-brain-reforms.summary: Tom returns home and tries to turn over a new leaf, while still using his brains on town troubles. J.D. watches the results.

the-return-of-the-great-brain.title: The Return of the Great Brain
the-return-of-the-great-brain.summary: Tom is back in Adenville and his schemes continue, as do his scrapes with the rest of the family. J.D. again recounts the chaos.

from-the-mixed-up-files-of-mrs-basil-e-f.title: From the Mixed-Up Files of Mrs. Basil E. Frankweiler
from-the-mixed-up-files-of-mrs-basil-e-f.summary: Claudia runs away from home with her little brother Jamie and hides in the Metropolitan Museum of Art. They get drawn into the mystery of a statue that may be a Michelangelo.
characters: Mrs. Frankweiler — wealthy, sharp-witted old woman

jennifer-hecate-macbeth-william-mckinley.title: Jennifer, Hecate, Macbeth, William McKinley, and Me, Elizabeth
jennifer-hecate-macbeth-william-mckinley.summary: Lonely new girl Elizabeth befriends Jennifer, who claims to be a witch. Elizabeth becomes her apprentice, with odd tasks and eventually a test of their friendship.
jennifer-hecate-macbeth-william-mckinley.setting: A small town in New York State, 1960s

father-s-arcane-daughter.title: Father's Arcane Daughter
father-s-arcane-daughter.summary: A girl long thought kidnapped suddenly returns to a wealthy family, and her half-brother and sister begin to wonder whether she is who she says. It is a quiet mystery about family and identity.

the-view-from-saturday.title: The View from Saturday
the-view-from-saturday.summary: Four sixth graders, chosen as a school Academic Bowl team, each have a hidden link to their teacher. The story unfolds from each of their viewpoints.

the-good-master.title: The Good Master
the-good-master.summary: Wild city girl Kate is sent to live on her uncle's Hungarian ranch, where she and her cousin Jancsi grow up together amid horses, festivals and the coming of war.

a-brand-new-uncle.title: A Brand-New Uncle
a-brand-new-uncle.summary: A sequel to the Hungarian ranch stories in which Kate and Jancsi's world is changed by a new family arrival and village adventure.
a-brand-new-uncle.note: May be Kate Seredy's 1941 'Listening' or a related title; verify. Likely 'A Brand-New Uncle' published 1961.

the-white-stag.title: The White Stag
the-white-stag.summary: This retells the legend of the Huns and Magyars and their migration from Asia to Europe led by a white stag. It covers the boyhood of Attila and the founding of Hungary.
the-white-stag.setting: Central Asia and Europe, ancient times

island-of-the-blue-dolphins.title: Island of the Blue Dolphins
island-of-the-blue-dolphins.summary: Karana is left alone on a Pacific island after her tribe leaves. She builds shelter, hunts, and befriends animals for years.

sing-down-the-moon.title: Sing Down the Moon
sing-down-the-moon.summary: Bright Morning, a young Navajo girl, tells of her people's forced march, the Long Walk, from their homeland.
characters: Tall Boy — young man she loves

the-king-s-fifth.title: The King's Fifth
the-king-s-fifth.summary: A young mapmaker joins a Spanish expedition seeking the golden cities of Cibola, and is later put on trial in Spain. The tale shows gold greed and its price.

charlotte-s-web.title: Charlotte's Web
charlotte-s-web.summary: Wilbur the pig is saved from slaughter by his friend Charlotte, a barn spider, who weaves words into her web to convince the farmer. It is about friendship and the cycle of life.
characters: Fern Arable — girl who saves Wilbur
charlotte-s-web.setting: A New England farm, mid-20th century

stuart-little.title: Stuart Little
stuart-little.summary: Stuart is a mouse born into a human family in New York. He sets out on a journey seeking a lost friend.
characters: Mr. and Mrs. Little — kind parents
stuart-little.setting: New York City and the countryside, 1940s

the-trumpet-of-the-swan.title: The Trumpet of the Swan
the-trumpet-of-the-swan.summary: Louis, a trumpeter swan born without a voice, learns to read and plays a trumpet to win a mate. A boy named Sam helps him.

maniac-magee.title: Maniac Magee
maniac-magee.summary: Orphaned Jeffrey Magee turns up in Two Mills, a town divided by race, and becomes a local legend. His search for a home stirs the town.

crash.title: Crash
crash.summary: Crash Coogan is a brash, football-obsessed seventh grader whose friendship with a gentle Quaker neighbor challenges him. When his grandfather is ill he grows.

who-put-that-hair-in-my-toothbrush.title: Who Put That Hair in My Toothbrush?
who-put-that-hair-in-my-toothbrush.summary: Siblings Greg and Megan, who constantly feud, tell their own versions of the same events. It is a funny look at family rivalry.

otherwise-known-as-sheila-the-great.title: Otherwise Known as Sheila the Great
otherwise-known-as-sheila-the-great.summary: Sheila Tubman, who brags and is afraid of many things, spends a summer in Tarrytown trying to hide her fears. She slowly learns to be honest with herself.
characters: Sheila Tubman — bold on the outside, anxious

tales-of-a-fourth-grade-nothing.title: Tales of a Fourth Grade Nothing
tales-of-a-fourth-grade-nothing.summary: Peter Hatcher is stuck with his mischievous little brother Fudge, who keeps causing chaos. The family's patience is tested.

onion-john.title: Onion John
onion-john.summary: Twelve-year-old Andy befriends Onion John, a local odd-job man, and the town tries to help in ways he does not want. It explores kindness and independence.

and-now-miguel.title: ...And Now Miguel
and-now-miguel.summary: Miguel, a New Mexico sheepherder's son, wants to go with the men to the Sangre de Cristo mountains. He must learn what that means.

the-way-to-sattin-shore.title: The Way to Sattin Shore
the-way-to-sattin-shore.summary: Kate Tranter lives with her grandmother and begins asking questions about her father, thought drowned. The answers lead her toward the truth.

who-s-afraid-and-other-strange-stories.title: Who's Afraid? and Other Strange Stories
who-s-afraid-and-other-strange-stories.summary: A collection of short stories mixing quiet menace and the supernatural, set in ordinary English life.

gaffer-samson-s-luck.title: Gaffer Samson's Luck
gaffer-samson-s-luck.summary: James is a newcomer to a Fen village who befriends old Gaffer Samson, and they share a story from the past. It deals with courage and friendship.

the-green-book.title: The Green Book
the-green-book.summary: Facing the end of Earth, a group of people and children leave on a spaceship to a new planet. They begin a hard new life, writing their story in a green book.

that-s-one-ornery-orphan.title: That's One Ornery Orphan
that-s-one-ornery-orphan.summary: Orphaned Hannah runs from a harsh orphanage and takes to the open range, with comic misadventures.

eight-mules-from-monterey.title: Eight Mules from Monterey
eight-mules-from-monterey.summary: A librarian and her family cross the California mountains on mules, bringing books to remote places.

the-black-stallion-and-satan.title: The Black Stallion and Satan
the-black-stallion-and-satan.summary: The Black and his young friend Alec face a wild stallion and a race.

the-black-stallion.title: The Black Stallion
the-black-stallion.summary: After a shipwreck, Alec Ramsay and a wild black stallion are stranded together on an island. They return home and train for a race.
the-black-stallion.setting: At sea, a desert island and New York, 1940s

missing-may.title: Missing May
missing-may.summary: Twelve-year-old Summer lives with Aunt May and Uncle Ob in West Virginia. After May's death, they find healing.
characters: Summer — orphan raised by Aunt and Uncle

the-van-gogh-cafe.title: The Van Gogh Cafe
the-van-gogh-cafe.summary: In a small Kansas town, a cafe in a former theater is a magical, healing place for the people who gather there.
characters: Clara — young girl in the cafe

gay-neck-the-story-of-a-pigeon.title: Gay-Neck: The Story of a Pigeon
gay-neck-the-story-of-a-pigeon.summary: A homing pigeon in India is trained by a boy, Ghond, flies through storms and through war with messages.
gay-neck-the-story-of-a-pigeon.setting: India and the Himalayas, early 20th century

the-door-in-the-wall.title: The Door in the Wall
the-door-in-the-wall.summary: Robin, a boy in medieval England, loses the use of his legs and must find new ways to serve his king.

peter-pan.title: Peter Pan
peter-pan.summary: Peter Pan and Wendy, John and Michael fly to Neverland, where they meet fairies, pirates and Lost Boys.
peter-pan.note: First staged as a play in 1904; novel published 1911 as Peter and Wendy.

only-earth-and-sky-last-forever.title: Only Earth and Sky Last Forever
only-earth-and-sky-last-forever.summary: Dark Elk, a Cheyenne youth, trains as a warrior and takes part in the events leading to the Battle of the Little Bighorn.

the-happiest-ending.title: The Happiest Ending
the-happiest-ending.summary: Twelve-year-old Rinko learns about love, family and an arranged marriage in a Japanese-American community in California.

miss-hickory.title: Miss Hickory
miss-hickory.summary: Miss Hickory is a doll with an applewood head who is left behind in New Hampshire. She survives a hard winter among animals.

roller-skates.title: Roller Skates
roller-skates.summary: Lucinda, ten, spends a year in 1890s New York City exploring on roller skates, making friends from all walks of life.

the-pushcart-war.title: The Pushcart War
the-pushcart-war.summary: New York City's pushcart owners, bullied by giant trucks, fight back with pea shooters. The satire is told as history.

incognito-mosquito-private-insective.title: Incognito Mosquito, Private Insective
incognito-mosquito-private-insective.summary: A mosquito detective tackles insect-world cases in a send-up of private-eye stories.
incognito-mosquito-private-insective.note: Little verifiable information; author full name uncertain.

magic-by-the-lake.title: Magic by the Lake
magic-by-the-lake.summary: Four siblings find a magical lake that grants wishes, leading to surprises on their holiday.
magic-by-the-lake.setting: A lake in the United States, 1950s

waterless-mountain.title: Waterless Mountain
waterless-mountain.summary: Younger Brother, a Navajo boy, grows up learning the ways of his people from his medicine-man uncle.
waterless-mountain.setting: Navajo country, American Southwest, early 20th century

haji-of-the-elephants.title: Haji of the Elephants
haji-of-the-elephants.summary: A boy in Asia cares for elephants and has adventures.
haji-of-the-elephants.note: Could not verify details or date.

a-long-vacation.title: A Long Vacation
a-long-vacation.summary: A group of schoolboys are carried away on a yacht and wrecked on an uninhabited island. They organize and survive, but tensions arise.
a-long-vacation.note: Original French title Deux ans de vacances (1888); also published as Two Years' Vacation.

sounder.title: Sounder
sounder.summary: A sharecropper's family in the Depression-era South faces hardship after the father is jailed. A boy and his dog Sounder endure.

ask-me-no-questions.title: Ask Me No Questions
ask-me-no-questions.summary: A children's story set in Victorian England.

an-american-ghost.title: An American Ghost
an-american-ghost.summary: A ghost story set in America.

the-dragons-of-blueland.title: The Dragons of Blueland
the-dragons-of-blueland.summary: Elmer Elevator, a boy, and his dragon Boris return to save dragons.

the-night-daddy.title: The Night Daddy
the-night-daddy.summary: Julia's mother works nights, so a young man comes to babysit.

dicey-s-song.title: Dicey's Song
dicey-s-song.summary: Dicey Tillerman and her siblings settle with their grandmother after being abandoned. They learn to belong.

the-story-of-king-arthur-and-his-knights.title: The Story of King Arthur and His Knights

april-raintree.title: In Search of April Raintree
april-raintree.summary: Two Metis sisters separated in foster care grow into very different women. It is about identity and prejudice.
characters: April Raintree — light-skinned, wants to pass
Cheryl Raintree — proud of her heritage
april-raintree.note: Notebook title shortened; a shortened edition was released as April Raintree (1984).

the-neverending-story.title: The Neverending Story
the-neverending-story.summary: Bastian, a bookish outsider, reads a book that pulls him into Fantastica.

some-things-strange-and-sinister.title: Some Things Strange and Sinister
some-things-strange-and-sinister.summary: An anthology of eerie tales for young readers.

the-red-badge-of-courage.title: The Red Badge of Courage
the-red-badge-of-courage.summary: Henry Fleming, a young Union soldier, faces fear in battle.

ghosts-a-classic-collection.title: Ghosts: A Classic Collection
ghosts-a-classic-collection.summary: A collection of classic ghost stories.

morning-girl.title: Morning Girl
morning-girl.summary: Morning Girl and her brother Star Boy live on a Bahamian island in 1492.

the-tale-of-pigling-bland-the-tale-of-mi.title: The Tale of Pigling Bland; The Tale of Miss Moppet; The Tale of Mr. Tod

shadows-and-whispers-tales-from-the-othe.title: Shadows and Whispers: Tales from the Other Side

free-land.title: Free Land
free-land.summary: A young couple homestead on the Dakota prairie.

seven-alone.title: Seven Alone
seven-alone.summary: Seven Sager children travel the Oregon Trail after losing their parents.

to-kill-a-mockingbird.title: To Kill a Mockingbird
to-kill-a-mockingbird.summary: Scout Finch narrates her childhood in Alabama as her father defends a Black man.

the-good-earth.title: The Good Earth
the-good-earth.summary: Wang Lung, a poor Chinese farmer, works and rises through hardship.

C. S. Lewis.bio: Lewis was an Oxford and Cambridge scholar of medieval literature. He wrote the Narnia books for children, partly inspired by children evacuated to his house in WWII. He was a close friend of J. R. R. Tolkien.

Charles Dickens.bio: Dickens was the greatest novelist of Victorian England. He worked in a factory as a boy when his father was imprisoned for debt, which shaped his books. His serial novels were immensely popular.

John D. Fitzgerald.bio: Fitzgerald based the Great Brain books on his own boyhood in Utah. He wrote them as a way to tell the stories of his childhood and his clever older brother.

E. L. Konigsburg.bio: Konigsburg won two Newbery awards, including for her first book. She trained as a chemist before writing for children and drew on her own family and her daughter's experiences.
known_for: From the Mixed-Up Files of Mrs. Basil E. Frankweiler

Kate Seredy.bio: Seredy was an illustrator who emigrated to the US in 1922. She drew on her childhood in Hungary for her books and illustrated them herself.

Scott O'Dell.bio: O'Dell wrote historical novels after a career as a screenwriter and journalist. He won the Newbery for Island of the Blue Dolphins and set up an award for historical fiction.

E. B. White.birthplace: Mount Vernon, New York, United States
E. B. White.bio: White was a New Yorker essayist and co-author of The Elements of Style. He wrote Charlotte's Web at his farm in Maine, inspired by a spider he watched in his barn.

Jerry Spinelli.bio: Spinelli wrote for adults at first, then turned to young readers while raising his children. He won the Newbery Medal for Maniac Magee.

Judy Blume.bio: Blume began writing while raising her kids. She is known for honest books on growing up and her Fudge stories.
known_for: Tales of a Fourth Grade Nothing
Are You There God? It's Me, Margaret

Joseph Krumgold.birthplace: Jersey City, New Jersey, United States
Joseph Krumgold.bio: Krumgold was a filmmaker who turned to children's novels. He won two Newbery Medals, the first author to do so.

Philippa Pearce.bio: Pearce grew up in a mill house in Cambridgeshire, which inspired Tom's Midnight Garden. She worked as a BBC scriptwriter and editor before writing.

Jill Paton Walsh.bio: Walsh was an English novelist who wrote for children and adults and finished Dorothy Sayers's Lord Peter novels. She was made a Fellow of the Royal Society of Literature.

Patricia Beatty.bio: Beatty wrote historical novels for young readers set mainly in the American West. She wrote many books, sometimes with her husband.

Walter Farley.bio: Farley wrote The Black Stallion while a student at Columbia University. It became the first of a long series.

Cynthia Rylant.bio: Rylant grew up in West Virginia Appalachian towns and worked as a librarian before writing. She has written picture books and novels.

Dhan Gopal Mukerji.bio: Mukerji moved to the US to study and became a writer. He wrote about India for American children, and was the first Asian-American Newbery winner.

Marguerite de Angeli.bio: De Angeli wrote and illustrated more than 30 books, often about families and history. She won the Newbery Medal for The Door in the Wall.

J. M. Barrie.bio: Barrie wrote plays and novels, and Peter Pan emerged from stories he told the Llewelyn Davies boys. He gave the rights to Great Ormond Street Hospital.

Nathaniel Benchley.bio: Benchley, son of humorist Robert Benchley and father of Peter Benchley, wrote novels and children's books.
known_for: Only Earth and Sky Last Forever

Yoshiko Uchida.bio: Uchida was interned with her family during WWII, an experience that shaped her writing about Japanese Americans.

Carolyn Sherwin Bailey.birthplace: Hoosick Falls, New York, United States
Carolyn Sherwin Bailey.bio: Bailey was a teacher and editor who wrote many books for young children. She won the Newbery for Miss Hickory.

Ruth Sawyer.bio: Sawyer was a storyteller who collected folk tales and won the Newbery for Roller Skates.

Jean Merrill.bio: Merrill wrote children's books and worked in publishing. The Pushcart War is her best-known work.

Edward Eager.bio: Eager was a playwright and lyricist who began writing children's books for his son, inspired by E. Nesbit.

Laura Adams Armer.bio: Armer was a photographer who lived among the Navajo and then wrote about them. She won the Newbery for Waterless Mountain.

Jules Verne.bio: Verne is a pioneer of science fiction, whose adventure novels have been translated widely.
known_for: Twenty Thousand Leagues Under the Sea
Around the World in Eighty Days

William H. Armstrong.bio: Armstrong was a teacher and farmer. He wrote Sounder, which won the Newbery Medal.

Ruth Stiles Gannett.bio: Gannett wrote My Father's Dragon at age 22 based on stories she heard from her father.

Maria Gripe.bio: Gripe was a Swedish author of children's novels and won the Hans Christian Andersen Award in 1974.

Cynthia Voigt.bio: Voigt was an English teacher who wrote the Tillerman cycle. She won the Newbery for Dicey's Song.

Howard Pyle.bio: Pyle was an illustrator and author who shaped the look of pirates and knights, and taught N. C. Wyeth.
known_for: The Merry Adventures of Robin Hood
The Story of King Arthur and His Knights

Beatrice Culleton.bio: Culleton Mosionier is a Metis author whose first novel drew on her foster care experience.

Michael Ende.bio: Ende was a German author whose fantasy novels were widely translated.

Joan Kahn.bio: Kahn was an editor of mystery fiction and anthologies.

Stephen Crane.bio: Crane was a journalist and novelist who wrote The Red Badge of Courage without having seen battle. He died young.

Michael Dorris.bio: Dorris was a writer and anthropologist of Modoc descent.
known_for: A Yellow Raft in Blue Water

Beatrix Potter.bio: Potter was a writer and illustrator who became a conservationist, giving land to the National Trust.

Rose Wilder Lane.birthplace: De Smet, Dakota Territory, United States
Rose Wilder Lane.bio: Lane was a journalist and the daughter of Laura Ingalls Wilder, whom she helped edit.

Honoré Morrow.bio: Morrow wrote historical novels and biographies.

Harper Lee.bio: Lee wrote To Kill a Mockingbird, drawing on her Alabama childhood. She was a friend of Truman Capote.

Pearl S. Buck.bio: Buck grew up in China as the daughter of missionaries. She won the Nobel Prize in Literature in 1938.
